statement: Once-weekly semaglutide 2.4 mg produces ~15% mean body-weight loss over 68 weeks in non-diabetic adults with obesity.
effect_size: -14.9% body weight vs -2.4% placebo at 68 weeks
population: 1,961 non-diabetic adults with overweight/obesity (STEP 1)
confidence_notes: Surrogate endpoint (weight), but a large, robust, randomized effect. Weight regains after discontinuation. ~25-40% of lost mass is lean — see semaglutide-muscle-loss-caveat. Domain S/D/E.

statement: In overweight/obese adults WITHOUT diabetes but with established cardiovascular disease, semaglutide 2.4 mg reduced major adverse cardiovascular events by ~20%.
effect_size: MACE HR 0.80 (~20% relative risk reduction); CV death/MI/stroke composite
population: 17,604 adults, overweight/obese, established CVD, no diabetes (SELECT)
confidence_notes: The pivotal HARD-OUTCOME result that reframed GLP-1s from weight drugs to cardiometabolic organ-protection drugs. Benefit partly independent of weight loss (curves separate early; mechanism still mechanistic). NOT a lifespan trial and NOT a general-population claim — enrolled high-risk patients. Domain S.

statement: Semaglutide 1.0 mg reduced major kidney-disease events by ~24% in patients with type 2 diabetes and chronic kidney disease.
effect_size: Major kidney events HR 0.76 (~24% RRR); trial stopped early for benefit
population: 3,533 with T2D + CKD (FLOW)
confidence_notes: Hard renal+CV+mortality outcome; extends GLP-1 organ-protection to the kidney. Disease population (T2D+CKD), not general longevity. Domain S.

statement: Tirzepatide (dual GIP/GLP-1 agonist) produces up to ~21% mean body-weight loss over 72 weeks in non-diabetic adults with obesity.
effect_size: -20.9% body weight at 15 mg vs -3.1% placebo at 72 weeks
population: 2,539 non-diabetic adults with obesity (SURMOUNT-1)
confidence_notes: Surrogate (weight), randomized, surgical-magnitude. Dual incretin appears more potent than semaglutide. Same muscle-loss caveat applies. Cardiovascular-outcome trial (SURMOUNT-MMO) pending at time of writing. Domain S/D/E.

statement: Roughly 25-40% of the weight lost on GLP-1 receptor agonists is lean (muscle) mass, not fat — a longevity-relevant caveat given that muscle mass/strength independently protect against mortality and frailty.
effect_size: ~25-40% of total weight lost is lean mass (DXA in GLP-1 weight-loss trials); typical of rapid weight loss generally
population: GLP-1 weight-loss trial body-composition substudies

provenance.primary: Body-composition substudies of STEP/SURMOUNT-class trials; rapid-weight-loss lean-mass literature

confidence_notes: MIXED: net metabolic benefit can coexist with erosion of mortality-protective muscle reserve. Mitigation (resistance training + >=1.2-1.6 g/kg protein) should be standard, not optional. Cross-ref Domain E (grip strength / VO2max mortality), 02-training.md, 03-nutrition-supplements.md.

statement: Statin therapy reduces major vascular events by ~22% per 1 mmol/L (~39 mg/dL) reduction in LDL cholesterol, per year of treatment.
effect_size: ~22% RRR in major vascular events per 1 mmol/L LDL reduction (CTT meta-analysis)
population: CTT Collaboration meta-analyses (>170,000 participants across statin RCTs)
confidence_notes: Highest-tier hard-outcome evidence; underwrites the apoB/LDL causal story (cross-ref L-biomarkers ldl-apob-causal-ascvd, apob-superior-to-ldlc; Ference 2017). Benefit tracks ABSOLUTE LDL reduction by any mechanism. Domain S/L.

statement: Statin absolute benefit depends on baseline risk: large in secondary prevention (NNT single-to-low-double digits over ~5y) and modest in low-risk primary prevention (NNT tens-to-hundreds), even though the relative risk reduction is similar.
effect_size: Secondary prevention NNT ~ single-to-low-double digits / 5y; primary prevention NNT ~ tens-to-hundreds / 5y (risk-dependent)
population: Statin RCT meta-analyses stratified by baseline risk

provenance.primary: CTT Collaboration meta-analyses; primary-prevention statin reviews

confidence_notes: NET-BENEFIT honesty: same pill, very different absolute value by population. Strong/uncontroversial in secondary prevention; shared-decision against modest absolute benefit in low-risk primary prevention. Domain S.

statement: Most reported statin muscle side effects are nocebo: in a blinded n-of-1 trial, ~90% of symptom burden occurred on placebo months too.
effect_size: ~90% of symptom intensity reproduced on placebo (SAMSON nocebo ratio); blinded RCTs show muscle-symptom rates barely above placebo
population: 60 patients with prior statin intolerance (SAMSON n-of-1)
confidence_notes: Refutes the popular 'statins commonly cause muscle damage' framing. Real myopathy exists but is rare; rhabdomyolysis ~1-3/100,000 pt-yr; small real increase in new-onset T2D outweighed by CV benefit in those who need it. Domain S.

statement: Adding ezetimibe to a statin after acute coronary syndrome further reduced cardiovascular events, proving non-statin LDL-lowering also delivers outcome benefit.
effect_size: Small further event reduction (HR ~0.936) over ~7 years on top of statin
population: 18,144 post-ACS patients (IMPROVE-IT)
confidence_notes: Modest absolute effect but mechanistically pivotal: confirmed 'lower LDL is better, by any mechanism.' Supports the apoB causal lever. Domain S/L.

statement: PCSK9 inhibition (evolocumab) added to statin lowered LDL to ~30 mg/dL and reduced major adverse cardiovascular events by ~15%.
effect_size: MACE ~15% RRR; LDL reduced ~59% to median ~30 mg/dL
population: 27,564 patients with atherosclerotic CVD on statin (FOURIER)
confidence_notes: Hard outcome; extends the 'lower-is-better' apoB curve to very low LDL safely. Cost/access limit use. Domain S/L.

statement: An intensive systolic blood-pressure target (<120 vs <140 mmHg) reduced major cardiovascular events ~25% and all-cause mortality ~27% in higher-risk non-diabetic adults, at the cost of more hypotension/AKI.
effect_size: MACE ~25% RRR; all-cause mortality ~27% RRR; increased hypotension, syncope, electrolyte disturbance, acute kidney injury
population: 9,361 higher-risk non-diabetic adults (SPRINT)
confidence_notes: Hard outcome; defines the modern lower-is-better BP target in the right patients, with monitoring. Measurement technique (unattended automated) and frailty caveats owned by clinical-prevention material. Cross-ref. Domain S.

statement: In healthy adults aged 70+ without established cardiovascular disease, daily low-dose aspirin did NOT improve disability-free survival or reduce CV events, significantly increased major bleeding, and showed slightly higher all-cause mortality.
effect_size: No disability-free-survival or CV benefit; major hemorrhage significantly increased; all-cause mortality slightly higher (cancer-driven)
population: 19,114 community-dwelling adults >=70 (>=65 US minorities), no CVD (ASPREE)
confidence_notes: Clean NEGATIVE: a 'stop doing this.' Net harm (bleeding > benefit) for primary prevention in healthy elders; guidelines revised. Does NOT apply to SECONDARY prevention (prior MI/stroke), where aspirin remains indicated. Companion papers 10.1056/NEJMoa1800722 (disability-free survival), 10.1056/NEJMoa1805819 (CV/bleeding). Domain S.

statement: Herpes zoster (shingles) vaccination is associated with lower subsequent dementia incidence, including in a quasi-experimental natural-experiment design (~20% relative reduction).
effect_size: ~20% relative reduction in new dementia diagnoses over 7y (Welsh eligibility-cutoff natural experiment); recombinant > live vaccine (Taquet)
population: Welsh zoster-eligibility cohort (natural experiment); large EHR cohorts

provenance.primary: Eyting, Geldsetzer et al., Nature 2025 (natural experiment); Taquet et al., Nat Med 2024

confidence_notes: Quasi-experimental (regression-discontinuity-like) design is closer to causal than ordinary cohort but is NOT a randomized trial; residual confounding not fully excluded. ADDS to (does not carry) the already-strong shingles-prevention case. Cross-ref brain/cognition material. Taquet 2024 = 10.1038/s41591-024-03201-5. Domain S.

statement: Influenza vaccination after myocardial infarction reduced cardiovascular death and events in a randomized trial — the flu shot acts partly as a cardiovascular intervention in at-risk people.
effect_size: Reduced composite of all-cause death, MI, stent thrombosis and CV death vs placebo post-MI
population: 2,571 patients with recent MI / high-risk CAD (IAMI)
confidence_notes: Randomized hard-outcome evidence that vaccination is underrated longevity/CV medicine. Flu is a known MI trigger. Domain S.

statement: Age-appropriate vaccination (pneumococcal, influenza, RSV, zoster) prevents leading infectious causes of older-adult death and hospitalization — a high-leverage, low-cost, strong-evidence longevity intervention.
effect_size: Substantial reductions in target-infection morbidity/mortality (pneumococcal, RSV, influenza, zoster)
population: Older-adult vaccine RCTs / programs

provenance.primary: Pivotal vaccine RCTs (Shingrix ZOE-50/70; RSV AReSVi-006/RENOIR; pneumococcal CAPiTA); program data

confidence_notes: Target-disease prevention is rock-solid rct-grade and is the baseline case; the dementia/CV 'bonus' signals (zoster-vaccine-dementia-signal, influenza-vaccine-cv-events) ADD to it. Domain S.

statement: Off-label metformin to slow human aging rests on confounded observational data and an unrun trial (TAME); there is no randomized human aging-outcome evidence, and it may blunt exercise adaptations.
effect_size: Bannister 2014 cohort signal is confounded (immortal-time/prevalent-user); TAME is a trial DESIGN, not a result; Konopka 2019 shows attenuated mitochondrial/aerobic training adaptation
population: Observational diabetic cohorts; small exercise-interaction RCTs

provenance.primary: Bannister 2014 (cohort); Barzilai TAME design 2016; Konopka et al. 2019 (exercise blunting)

confidence_notes: Cross-ref Domain B (metformin/TAME). EXPERIMENTAL/off-label for aging. Exercise-blunting makes the trade-off wrong-way-round for a healthy athletic person. Predictor (glucose/AMPK) != lever (lifespan). Domain S/B.

statement: Rapamycin is the strongest mouse-lifespan drug known, but the human anti-aging dose, schedule, and long-term safety are unknown; the best human data are surrogate (improved vaccine response).
effect_size: Mouse median lifespan +9-14% (Harrison 2009); human rapalog improved elderly flu-vaccine titer (Mannick 2014, surrogate); optimal human regimen unknown
population: ITP mice (lifespan); elderly humans (vaccine-response RCT)

provenance.primary: Harrison et al. Nature 2009; Mannick et al. Sci Transl Med 2014; PEARL off-label data

confidence_notes: Cross-ref Domain B (mTOR/rapamycin). Off-label/experimental for healthspan; immunosuppression + metabolic side effects real. Bryan Johnson discontinued (J-claims bj-rapamycin-discontinued). animal lifespan + rct surrogate, NOT human aging outcome. Domain S/B.

statement: SGLT2 inhibitors (empagliflozin, dapagliflozin) reduce cardiovascular death, heart-failure hospitalization, and renal decline in randomized trials — proven for heart failure and CKD (including many non-diabetics); the geroprotector hypothesis is plausible but unproven.
effect_size: Reduced CV death/HF hospitalization and slowed renal decline (EMPA-REG, DAPA-HF, DAPA-CKD, EMPA-KIDNEY)
population: Large HF/CKD/diabetes RCTs (tens of thousands)
confidence_notes: The only 'geroprotector-adjacent' drug with genuine hard human outcomes — but for DISEASE (HF/CKD), not aging per se. The aging/ketone-signaling geroprotector claim is mechanistic only. Domain S.

statement: Acarbose extends mouse lifespan in the rigorous Interventions Testing Program, especially in males, but has no human aging-outcome trial.
effect_size: Mouse median lifespan extension (sex-skewed toward males) in the ITP
population: ITP genetically heterogeneous mice

provenance.primary: Harrison et al., Aging Cell 2014 (ITP acarbose)

confidence_notes: animal lifespan only; no human aging trial. GI side effects (flatulence) limit use. Experimental for aging. Domain S/B.

statement: Testosterone replacement at physiologic doses did not increase major adverse cardiovascular events in middle-aged/older hypogonadal men with high cardiovascular risk (non-inferior CV safety).
effect_size: MACE non-inferior vs placebo; small increases in atrial fibrillation, pulmonary embolism, acute kidney injury
population: ~5,200 hypogonadal men 45-80 with high CV risk (TRAVERSE)
confidence_notes: Settles the long-standing CV-safety worry for replacement-dose TRT in symptomatic hypogonadism. NOT a longevity drug for normal-T men; lifestyle (sleep, weight loss, resistance training) addresses much age-related decline. Supraphysiologic/aesthetic dosing is a different, worse risk profile. Domain S/N.

statement: TRT is medicine for confirmed symptomatic hypogonadism (low measured testosterone PLUS symptoms), not a validated longevity intervention for men with normal-range testosterone.
effect_size: Improves libido, sexual function, body composition, bone density in genuine hypogonadism; no demonstrated longevity benefit in eugonadal men
population: Hypogonadal men (TTrials and related RCTs)

provenance.primary: Snyder et al., TTrials NEJM 2016; endocrine-society guidance

confidence_notes: Indication boundary: replacing a confirmed deficiency = medicine; pushing a normal/eugonadal man's T up to chase youth = experimentation, often medicalizing normal aging. Domain S.

statement: Levothyroxine provided no symptom or quality-of-life benefit for older adults with subclinical hypothyroidism, whereas it is clearly beneficial for overt hypothyroidism.
effect_size: No improvement in hypothyroid symptoms or tiredness vs placebo in subclinical disease (TRUST)
population: 737 adults >=65 with subclinical hypothyroidism (TRUST)
confidence_notes: Treat overt disease; resist medicating a borderline TSH or chasing 'optimal thyroid' in someone who feels well. Thyroid hormone is not a weight/energy drug for the euthyroid. Domain S.

statement: BPC-157 and TB-500 (gray-market 'healing/anti-aging' peptides) have essentially no controlled human efficacy or safety data; enthusiasm rests on rodent studies, and they are not FDA-approved pharmaceutical-grade products.
effect_size: Rodent tendon/gut-healing signals only; no human RCT; unknown source purity; FDA restricted BPC-157 from compounding
population: Rodent models; no controlled human trials

provenance.primary: Preclinical BPC-157/TB-4 literature; FDA 503A/503B bulk-substance actions

confidence_notes: animal/anecdotal tier; NO human outcome data, NO regulatory safety assurance. Indexed to be gradeable, NOT endorsed. Injecting unregulated research chemicals carries real risk. Domain S.

statement: Growth-hormone-secretagogue peptides (ipamorelin, GHRPs, sermorelin) raise the GH/IGF-1 axis — a surrogate that, per the best human and animal longevity genetics, points the WRONG way for lifespan (low IGF-1 signaling is associated with longevity).
effect_size: May raise GH/IGF-1 (surrogate); robust longevity genetics (Laron/low-IGF-1, daf-2, Ames/Snell dwarf mice) associate LOW IGF-1 signaling with longer life
population: Human GH-axis pharmacology + longevity genetics (Domains B/C)

provenance.primary: GH/IGF-1 longevity genetics (Bartke; Guevara-Aguirre & Longo 2011); GH-secretagogue pharmacology

confidence_notes: Mechanism sold as anti-aging outcome that contradicts the best aging biology. Raising GH/IGF-1 'to stay young' runs against the IIS/daf-2 longevity axis (Domain B IGF-1/insulin; Domain C). No human outcome data for these peptides regardless. Domain S/B/C.
